findings.title: A linked life-course under comprehensive and inward knowledge
findings.claim: The Hour, rain, hidden gestation, each self’s next-day acquisition, and its unknown death-ground can be read as linked phases of a life-course whose full trajectory is with God, not as five unrelated secrets.
findings.mechanism: The opening locative عنده frames knowledge as held with God; the focus then moves through sent rain, womb contents, two negated human knowing clauses, acquisition tomorrow, and death in an unspecified land, before closing with al-ʿAlīm and al-Khabīr. Wider supplied scenes connect womb contents to measure (13:8), tomorrow to intended action and self-examination (18:23; 59:18), death to an appointed term and an unavoidable meeting (3:145; 62:8), and the Hour to resurrection (22:7). The Creator-knows-what-He-created pairing in 67:14 returns to the closing khabīr.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can perceive the catalogue as a connected trajectory through time, provision, formation, personal action, and endpoint, while the repeated human not-knowing remains intact.
findings.containment: This links the listed domains without claiming that people cannot act, plan, learn local facts, or affect outcomes. The target verses supply Arabic but not target morphology, so no additional lexical analysis is inferred from them.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run finding is trusted and its focus anchors are resolved; the whole-life-course integration is still an interpretive synthesis, and connection targets lack morphology.

findings.title: Rain and womb as material forms of sustaining mercy
findings.claim: The focus places sent rain beside wombs; wider rain-after-despair and womb-development scenes let these remain literal weather and anatomy while opening two material ways life is relieved and carried.
findings.mechanism: In 42:28, rain comes after despair and is joined to the spreading of mercy; in 30:24, water revives earth after its death. The focus’s غيث therefore contacts both the rain and relief branches. The womb word contacts the core womb and kinship branches, while 13:8 and 22:5 describe carrying, change, and a measured term. These separate triggers return through the focus rain, sending, and womb carriers.
findings.reader_payoff: Rain is perceptible as provision received in need, and the womb as a sustaining interior tied to kinship and care, rather than the terms remaining isolated meteorology and anatomy.
findings.containment: The rain word does not cease to mean rain, and wombs do not lexically mean mercy or kinship in this clause. The wider scenes add a bounded resonance; they do not collapse the two processes into one.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding is directly supported by supplied wider Arabic, while the mercy/kinship synthesis remains contextual.

findings.title: Tomorrow as an open horizon for each self’s acquisition
findings.claim: A self may set out toward tomorrow and acquire benefit, yet the focus’s repeated negation denies that intention or effort lets it know or control what it will gain.
findings.mechanism: The focus places the indefinite self as subject of two تَدْرِى denials, with كَسَبَ directed to غَدًا. The independent future-action wording of 18:23 and self-examination for tomorrow in 59:18 meet that near horizon; 6:164 separately says a self earns against itself. The morning/departure branch is retained only analogically: an action aimed at tomorrow can feel like setting out, while the result remains open.
findings.reader_payoff: The future is not empty or passive: a person can act toward it, but cannot turn that reach into assured foreknowledge or ownership of the outcome.
findings.containment: The focus does not condemn planning, work, or intention, and the analogical departure image does not replace the ordinary ‘tomorrow’ sense. No claim is made that every acquisition is material rather than moral.

epistemic.reason: The core claim has trusted focus anchors and direct supplied future-action parallels; the departure image is bounded and analogical.

branch_activations.carrier: The first تَدْرِى is the knowledge denied to each self.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 18:23 cautions against claiming certainty about one’s action tomorrow; 59:18 directs each self to inspect what it sent ahead for tomorrow.
branch_activations.activation: The target scenes put future-directed agency beside the focus denial, so the same verb is felt as a limit on certainty rather than on action.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The self acts into a future it cannot fully know.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not erase possible ordinary estimates about likely outcomes.

findings.title: A familiar ground whose death-place remains unknown
findings.claim: A person inhabits and uses the earth and can direct action toward places, yet cannot know which ground will receive their death; wider death-and-renewal scenes let that unknown place also resonate with the earth’s own return to life.
findings.mechanism: The focus asks by which land a self will die and repeats the negated knowing verb. In 3:145 death occurs at a written term; in 62:8 the death people flee meets them. In 22:5 and 30:24 earth is joined to human development, death, rain, and revival. Thus the focus land word contacts both practical ground and a wider receiving ground, while the death verb contacts an earth-after-death image.
findings.reader_payoff: Ground remains the setting humans can occupy, but its relation to a person’s end is not available as a chosen or forecastable destination; the same earth can also be imagined as receiving renewal.
findings.containment: The focus does not say that a person cannot travel or choose an ordinary destination. The target verses’ morphology is not supplied, and the fertile/dead-earth readings are contextual analogies, not translations of the focus phrase.

epistemic.reason: The focus claim is trusted; the fertile-ground and dead-earth extensions are supported by supplied target Arabic but remain analogical.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The death-place belongs to the same earth that sustains and can be revived.

findings.title: A self’s course is not transferable
findings.claim: The repeated focus self and its acquisition become a particular, nontransferable bearer: gratitude benefits its doer, while the closest kin cannot occupy that self’s place at the final reckoning.
findings.mechanism: 31:12 says grateful action benefits the actor’s own self; 31:33 denies parent-child substitution in both directions; 6:164 independently says each self earns against itself and no burden-bearer carries another’s burden. These three triggers return through the focus self and acquisition.
findings.reader_payoff: The two future clauses feel not only unknown but personally attached to each bearer, from its acts to its endpoint.
findings.containment: The reading does not deny kinship, care, or shared responsibility in ordinary life; it limits only substitution and transferred accounting. HFT context roots/indices are attributed.

epistemic.reason: The exact context Arabic and cross-ayah text are supplied, but HFT segmentation and the extension from accountability to the focus trajectory remain attributed.

findings.title: Generative descent as an explicitly bounded material analogy
findings.claim: A surprising analogy can place rain’s downward transfer beside hidden generative reception: water and growth in 31:10 meet the focus’s adjacent rain and womb, without making rain lexically mean reproductive fluid.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies a descent verb and wombs; 31:10 supplies water followed by growth. HFT nominates a male-fluid branch under descent and a water/growth-to-generation bridge. The contact is retained as an attributed analogy because its carrier, independent growth trigger, focus return, and materially changed image are all named, while exact Arabic in 31:10 names water and plant growth only.
findings.reader_payoff: The physical pattern of descending provision received in a concealed interior and followed by life becomes visible as a secondary image alongside the ordinary rain reading.
findings.containment: This is exploratory and analogical only: 31:10 does not say semen, the focus rain word still means rain, and the HFT root/word-index mapping for 31:10 lacks independent target morphology.

epistemic.reason: The outlier has exact supplied Arabic and a complete attributed trace, but the reproductive-fluid relation is a branch-distant analogy rather than an independently established lexical sense.
